title: Parachute plan + handoff notes: Marcus Bellamy
content:
TLDR: Marcus Bellamy — strong systems engineer with GPU infra experience, pragmatic tradeoff thinking, good at debugging live systems. Interview panel split: 3 green / 1 yellow (operational rigour). Main risks: limited exposure to multi-tenant billing/quotas and sparse experience with policy rollouts. Suggested path: hire with an explicit 60-day parish/probe ramp (detailed below) and two focused mini-projects to validate scaling judgement and rollout discipline.

Candidate snapshot:
- Role interviewed for: Senior Runtime Engineer (serving/runtime infra)
- Background: 6 yrs infra (distributed systems), last 3 yrs focused on ML infra at mid-stage startup, shipped batching and KV cache improvements, helped debug degraded latency under load.
- Interview vibe: calm, systematic, leans to engineering-first answers, provides concrete triage threads. Good communicator but occasionally defers on product-level tradeoffs.

Strengths (evidence):
- Incident debugging: described a production P0 where they traced a tail-latency regression to a regressed kernel selector; proposed measurable mitigation and postmortem — panel liked the T-shaped debugging notes. (Panel note: Marcus walked us through logs -> bisection -> fix, including good rollback criteria.)
- Throughput/latency tradeoffs: solid instincts around batching and KV cache retention policies; suggested a small choke-point metric set to balance latency and GPU utilization.
- Mentoring and docs: has experience running triage sessions and writing runbooks; concrete examples provided.

Concerns / open questions (risk map):
- Rollouts & guardrails: less ownership history for multi-tenant quota enforcement and automated fallback policies (our main production differentiator). Needs explicit exposure to our rollout flows and failure modes.
- Model versioning nuance: has theoretical knowledge but limited hands-on with model cataloging + compatibility routing (we should verify via a short pairing exercise).
- Compensation expectation: asked for mid-senior band; confirm comp band and relocation/remote arrangement before offering.

Interview snippets to cite in reference: (copy-pasteable)
- "When I saw the tail-latency spike, I narrowed it to a kernel selection change and added a canary circuit to fail back to the prior selector if p95 > 300ms for 5 minutes."
- "My rule of thumb is: if a micro-optimisation increases cognitive overhead for the oncall by X, model it as a cost to weigh vs perf win."

Decision options (suggested):
1) Green hire with structured 60-day verification and dedicated mentor (preferred).
2) Conditional hire: same as (1) but with a 90-day formal review gate requiring evidence on rollout automation and quota controls.
3) No hire: if comp/expectations mismatch or references reveal operational gaps.

Parachute / first-90-day plan (practical checks to validate and ramp Marcus quickly):
- Week 0 (offer -> accept)
  - Send a short tech setup guide, ask candidate to do the onboarding checklist, create credentials for sandbox cluster.
  - Assign mentor: Connor Lee (serving runtime eng).
- Weeks 1–2 - Pair on a small production-readiness task: reproduce a simple regressions test that simulates a kernel selector flip. Deliverable: short doc + runbook for automatic rollback threshold.
  - Shadow current oncall and sit in two postmortem reviews.
- Weeks 3–6 - Mini-project A (scaling judgement): evaluate an existing batching config across two traffic shapes; propose a change, run an A/B test in staging, measure p50/p95 and cost delta. Deliverable: experiment notes, KPI dashboard snapshot.
  - Mini-project B (rollout/guardrail): implement a simple quota enforcement probe and a fallback policy in sandbox; add unit/integration tests and a playbook for paging fallback. Deliverable: PR and runbook.
- Weeks 7–12 - Ownership handoff: take on one low-risk production service (routing or a small model variant pool) with mentor oversight; own the next minor release and rollout plan.
  - 60-day check-in: present outcomes of mini-project A/B and rollout probe to the runtime team, include lessons learned and follow-ups.

Measurement criteria (to pass the verification gate):
- Demonstrated ability to design and execute an experiment that changed batching/cache config with measurable improvements and safe rollback.
- Delivered a rollout playbook that includes automated guards (alert thresholds + automatic fallback) and at least one integration test covering the fallback path.
- Clean handoffs and clear runbook updates for the service they own.

Suggested pairing interview follow-ups (if we want more data before offer):
- 90-minute live exercise: design a rollout flow for a new model variant with multi-tenant quotas and an automated rollback. Focus on alerting, metrics, and low-touch operator controls.
- Take-home: short analysis of a past incident (we provide logs and a timeline) asking for root cause, short remediations, and a rollout checklist.

Reference checks to ask about specifically:
- Examples of times they introduced automation that reduced oncall toil and how they measured impact.
- Situations where they had to make a rollback decision under ambiguity and what criteria they used.

Notes for hiring committee / packet blurb (one-liner):
Marcus is a pragmatic senior infra engineer who can debug complicated runtime regressions and ship measurable performance experiments quickly; we should validate hands-on rollout automation before fully trusting them with multi-tenant guardrails.

Admin / misc:
- Candidate timezone: PST; preferred start: 2025-01-06 earliest.
- Compensation asked: mid-senior band (range quoted verbally). Confirm total comp with People Ops.

Immediate next steps (for me):
- If we greenlight: draft offer language + attach this parachute plan as a start-of-First-90 action list.
- If we need more evidence: schedule the 90-minute live exercise with panelists (Connor, Nora, Maya).

Notes to self: keep the first project intentionally small and reversible. Emphasize measurable success criteria so the 60-day check-in is objective.

End of notes.
